tail:
ALLEGATION_VERDICT: REAL_NONFATAL
ALLEGATION_LOCATION: items/ex-an-aleph-fixed-point.md line 87, Verification step 1.1
ALLEGATION_ITEM_QUOTE: “Apply [L2] to the rule sending a function $h$ whose domain is an ordinal to”
ALLEGATION_TARGET_QUOTE: “Let $G$ be a **class function**: a rule, given by a formula in the language of set theory, that assigns a set $G(h)$ to every function $h$ whose domain is an ordinal ([[def-ordinal]]).”
ALLEGATION_REASONING: The judge correctly identifies that the displayed rule is not total on arbitrary ordinal-domain functions: a range may contain nonordinals, so its union need not be an ordinal and cannot index the aleph operation. This is nonfatal under the 30-second rule. Define G(h) to use the displayed aleph value when the union of the range is an ordinal and aleph-zero otherwise. Every output is then an ordinal, so along the resulting recursion the fallback is never used and all subsequent calculations remain valid.

QUOTE: “[L8] A cardinal is infinite exactly when”

EVIDENCE: The cited target’s relevant Statement is “**(b)** Every infinite cardinal is a limit ordinal ([[def-limit-ordinal]]).” The exact finite-versus-infinite definition occurs instead in def-cardinal-arithmetic, which this item does not directly declare or cite.
